cases.scenario: Response order reflects admin-set sortOrder then name, never pure alphabetical
cases.preconditions: Needs >=2 category fixtures with a deliberately non-alphabetical sortOrder to distinguish sortOrder-based order from alphabetical order; fixtures.json has no /categories entries at all today
cases.test_data: No category fixtures recorded in fixtures.json
cases.steps: GET /categories; compare the returned order of two categories with known non-alphabetical sortOrder values against a plain alphabetical sort
cases.response_assertions: array order equals sortOrder asc, name asc - NOT alphabetical-by-name when sortOrder differs
cases.business_outcome: Ordering is deliberate admin-curated sortOrder (BRI-356), not an alphabetical default
cases.expected: Order matches categories.repository.ts:17-19 orderBy + docs/features/taxonomy-tree.md:74
cases.blocked_reason: No category fixtures exist in fixtures.json; none recorded with a deliberately non-alphabetical sortOrder to distinguish the rule from a coincidentally-alphabetical result
cases.source: audit EP-033 suggested scenario #2; categories.repository.ts:9-19; docs/features/taxonomy-tree.md:74 (BRI-356)

cases.scenario: A legacy/off-tree category (e.g. 'Boots', 'Shirts & Tops') coexisting with the curated Women/Men/Kids/Gear tree is still returned unfiltered by GET /categories - conflicts with the sheet's implied 'curated tree only' framing
cases.preconditions: Code comments (categories.repository.ts:24-29, embeddings.service.ts:236-239) describe legacy categories coexisting with the curated tree in at least QA data at the time written (medium confidence, not independently confirmed against a live DB); no legacy/off-tree category fixture recorded in fixtures.json
cases.test_data: No legacy/off-tree category fixture recorded in fixtures.json
cases.steps: GET /categories; check whether a known legacy/off-tree category id is present in the array
cases.expected: Unclear/Conflict - do not assert pass/fail on whether legacy categories should be excluded until BA/PO clarify; code has no exclusion logic today
cases.blocked_reason: CF-033-02: sheet's title implies only customer-facing/curated-tree categories should appear; code has no exclusion logic and code comments (categories.repository.ts:24-29, embeddings.service.ts:236-239) describe legacy categories coexisting in at least QA data (medium confidence); also no legacy-category fixture exists to test against. Needs BA/PO clarification before asserting expected behaviour.
cases.source: audit EP-033 suggested scenario #4; Source agreement matrix row 'Legacy categories excluded from the public list'; categories.repository.ts:24-29; embeddings.service.ts:236-239

cases.scenario: A category deleted via admin DELETE (0 listings referencing it) no longer appears in GET /categories
cases.preconditions: Needs an admin account and a category fixture with zero listings referencing it, to delete via DELETE /admin/taxonomy/categories/:id then re-GET /categories; destructive, multi-step action
cases.test_data: No admin account or zero-listing category fixture currently provisioned in fixtures.json
cases.steps: 1) Admin DELETE /admin/taxonomy/categories/:id (category has 0 listings) -> expect 200/204. 2) GET /categories -> expect the deleted id absent from the array
cases.response_assertions: deleted category id not present in the subsequent GET /categories array
cases.business_outcome: Hard delete (admin.service.ts:614-624) permanently removes a category from the public flat list when it has no referencing listings
cases.expected: Category permanently absent from GET /categories after a successful admin hard-delete
cases.blocked_reason: Needs an admin account and a category fixture with zero listings to safely hard-delete; none provisioned in fixtures.json. Destructive, multi-step sequence - not a single Schemathesis call.
cases.source: audit EP-033 suggested scenario #5; admin.service.ts:614-624 (deleteCategory)

cases.scenario: A category still referenced by >=1 listing cannot be deleted (409) and therefore keeps appearing in GET /categories
cases.preconditions: Needs an admin account and a category fixture referenced by >=1 listing; none provisioned in fixtures.json
cases.test_data: No admin account or listing-referenced category fixture currently provisioned
cases.steps: 1) Admin DELETE /admin/taxonomy/categories/:id (category has >=1 listing) -> expect 409. 2) GET /categories -> expect the category still present
cases.response_assertions: 409 body names the listing count (countListingsInCategory); category id still present in the subsequent GET /categories array
cases.business_outcome: admin.service.ts:614-624 refuses hard-delete while listings reference the category (data-integrity rule), with the side effect that the category keeps appearing publicly with no way to hide it
cases.expected: 409 on delete attempt; category remains visible in GET /categories afterward
cases.blocked_reason: Needs an admin account and a category fixture referenced by at least one listing; none provisioned in fixtures.json. Multi-step sequence, not a single Schemathesis call.
cases.source: audit EP-033 suggested scenario #6; admin.service.ts:614-624 (countListingsInCategory 409 guard)
